questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. What does this mean?
questions.explanation: A solid line on the edge of the road marks the boundary between the travel lane and shoulder. When this line angles toward the center of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What do pentagon-shaped signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Pentagon-shaped signs mark school zones. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians when driving in these areas.

questions.question: When must you pull over and let an emergency vehicle pass?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This is required whether the vehicle is behind you or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beams so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, allow oncoming vehicles at least half of the main road. Both vehicles need enough space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body process in one hour?
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one drink per hour. However, how drunk you become depends on many factors: how much you drink, how fast you drink, your body weight, whether you have eaten, and your overall health.

questions.question: What do some highways use to guide drivers into the correct turning lanes?

options.text: White lines on the edge of the road.
White arrows painted in the middle of lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows painted in the middle of lanes.
questions.explanation: White arrows on the road show which lanes to use for turning or going straight.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a green light, but traffic is coming. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the edge of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Move into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
Turn now because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with approaching traffic, enter the intersection if the light is green. Wait in the center of the intersection until traffic clears, then turn.

questions.question: You are in traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure you have room to cross completely without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure you have room to cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before entering the tracks, check that you have enough space to get all the way across. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it as a warning and continue through.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light, slow down and try to stop before entering the intersection. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: Your car has Anti-Lock Brakes and starts to lose grip on a slippery road. What should you do?

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: If you lose traction, press down hard on the brake pedal and keep holding it. Steer toward safety. The Anti-Lock Braking System automatically pumps your brakes faster than you could. Releasing pressure or pumping the brakes will turn off the system.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a highway, turn into or out of a driveway, or make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is most important?

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, you must let pedestrians and oncoming vehicles go first.

questions.question: What color are signs for public recreation areas?
questions.explanation: Brown signs show cultural, historical, and recreation areas. They help you find places when traveling in new locations.

questions.question: When does your stopping distance increase?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: What do round signs warn you about?
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you that a railroad crossing is ahead. Drive with extra caution near railroad crossings.

questions.question: An oncoming car is heading straight at you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.

questions.explanation: Honk your horn to alert the other driver. Steer right to escape. If the other driver swerves left at the last second and you swerved left too, you will still crash. Brake hard and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You may turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. You must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a crossroad is coming up.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road facing the traffic coming toward you. This lets you see oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should your front wheels turn?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb.
Turn them slightly to the right.
Turn them sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic instead of into it.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on your left at an unmarked intersection and you arrive at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing where the tracks are at a steep angle. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should your wheels turn?
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road. If your vehicle rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What type of sign is diamond-shaped?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and usually yellow. Orange warning signs are used in work areas. These signs warn you about hazards ahead or special rules.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate lanes where traffic moves in opposite directions.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers let you through.
Drive around the rear of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting. If another vehicle hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead turns at a sharp angle.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead turns at a sharp angle.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply (in this case, to the right). Slow down before the sharp turn, just as you would at an intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and can expect oncoming traffic to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.
